title: MSCI Rejig Adds Laurus Labs, Groww, Adani Energy and Lenskart to Global Index
excerpt: Astral, Balkrishna Industries and SBI Card dropped from the MSCI India Standard Index in the August 2026 rebalancing, with changes effective August 31.
body:
• Laurus Labs, Groww, Adani Energy Solutions and Lenskart added to the MSCI India Standard Index in the August 2026 rejig announced on August 12.
  • Astral, Balkrishna Industries (BKT) and SBI Card dropped from the index, triggering estimated passive outflows of $138–$167 million each.
  • The rebalancing is expected to drive $2.3–$3.2 billion in net passive inflows into Indian equities when changes take effect on August 31.
  • India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index has declined over the past two years, making each index reshuffle carry greater flow implications.

MSCI announced the results of its August 2026 quarterly index review on Tuesday, adding Laurus Labs, Groww, Adani Energy Solutions and Lenskart to its widely tracked India Standard Index while removing Astral, Balkrishna Industries and SBI Cards and Payment Services.

The changes, which take effect at the close of August 31, are set to trigger billions of dollars in passive fund flows as global index-tracking ETFs and institutional portfolios rebalance their holdings to match the updated benchmark.

Who Got In

Among the additions, fintech platform Groww is expected to attract the largest passive inflows at roughly $821 million, according to JM Financial estimates published ahead of the announcement. Adani Energy Solutions, the power transmission arm of the Adani Group, could see approximately $342 million in index-linked buying.

Laurus Labs, the specialty pharmaceutical company, was widely seen as a high-probability candidate for migration from the MSCI India Small Cap Index to the Standard Index after its market capitalization surged on the back of strong CDMO earnings. The company reported a 126% year-on-year jump in consolidated net profit to ₹362 crore in Q1 FY27, with EBITDA margins expanding to 31.8%.

Lenskart, the eyewear retailer that went public in recent years, also made the cut as a fresh entrant to the global benchmark.

Who Got Dropped

Astral, the building products manufacturer, had been flagged as the highest-probability exclusion candidate due to a decline in its free-float adjusted market capitalization. SBI Cards, India's second-largest credit card issuer, was removed despite posting a 20% year-on-year profit increase in Q1 FY27 — its free-float market cap had been under sustained pressure. Balkrishna Industries, the off-highway tire maker, rounded out the exclusions.

JM Financial estimated passive outflows of $138 million for Astral, $146 million for SBI Cards and $167 million for Balkrishna Industries as index-tracking funds sell down their positions.

Why It Matters for Investors

The MSCI India Standard Index is one of the most closely watched benchmarks for global capital allocation into Indian equities. Nearly $17 trillion in assets were benchmarked to MSCI indexes globally at the end of 2024, with roughly $2 trillion in equity ETFs directly linked to them.

"Historical evidence suggests 8–15% cumulative excess returns in the 20 trading days preceding MSCI announcements for high-conviction inclusion candidates."

— JM Financial Research

India's weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index has declined over the past two years, even as the country's domestic equity markets have climbed. That makes each quarterly rebalancing carry outsized significance for flows — a dynamic JM Financial has repeatedly highlighted.

The Broader Picture

The August rejig is part of MSCI's regular quarterly review across its global index family. The MSCI ACWI (All Country World Index) is also seeing additions and deletions across developed and emerging markets, with the results impacting passive funds worldwide.

For Indian markets, the net effect is firmly positive. On aggregate, the high-probability inclusions and exclusions are expected to drive net passive inflows of roughly $2.3 billion to $3.2 billion into Indian equities, providing a tailwind for the added stocks heading into September.

Investors typically begin positioning ahead of the effective date, and elevated trading volumes in the included and excluded names are expected over the next three weeks before the August 31 implementation.
nri_angle: MSCI index changes directly affect NRI and global investors holding India-linked ETFs and passive funds, with billions in flows at stake.
